contract: F-11, the updates/update.log lines of the import (app-update task T6.0b; record docs/app-updates.md 4.5 "update.log events of the import", 3.5, 5.3 "The app's lines"): the five events P6 registers in UPDATE_LOG_EVENTS, each key in a fixed order with one token rule or a closed list. The frame, the time and the token rules V, I, E and C are vectors.json's; this file adds the five events and their vectors. Written from the record before the events were registered

rules.code: closed: the 26 codes an import answers, from table B.9: UPD-NOT-AVAILABLE, UPD-NOT-A-DRIVE, UPD-POLICY-MANAGED, UPD-POLICY-INVALID, UPD-IN-PROGRESS, UPD-DRIVE-READ-ONLY, UPD-DRIVE-FULL, UPD-TOO-NEW, UPD-FILE-DAMAGED, UPD-NOT-GENUINE, UPD-UNKNOWN-SIGNER, UPD-FOR-NEWER-HILBERTRAUM, UPD-NOT-AN-UPDATE, UPD-WRONG-CHANNEL, UPD-NEEDS-IN-BETWEEN, UPD-SAME-OR-OLDER, UPD-ABOVE-MAX-VERSION, UPD-CANT-CHECK-LINUX-FLOOR, UPD-OS-TOO-OLD, UPD-DOWNLOAD-INCOMPLETE, UPD-NO-HELPER, UPD-PATH-TOO-LONG, UPD-FILE-TOO-BIG-FOR-DRIVE, UPD-CANT-READ-FILE, UPD-CANT-WRITE-DRIVE, UPD-OLD-FILE
rules.version: V, with the sentinel `unknown` for a version of 25 to 64 bytes; present when the run knows the update's version (an accepted payload, or the refusal's own version parameter: UPD-SAME-OR-OLDER, UPD-ABOVE-MAX-VERSION), else left out
rules.stale_drive_version: closed: yes, no; present when the run reached checkPayload
rules.err: E: the thrown error's code, for the codes an I/O error gives; left out when none was thrown or it fails E
rules.syscall: C: the thrown error's bare system call; left out when none was thrown or it fails C
rules.link: closed: updates, staging, version, incoming, probe; with UPD-CANT-WRITE-DRIVE only

rules.files: I: the `files[]` members staged, member 0 not counted

rules.version: as import-refused; present when the payload was accepted before the cancel

rules.n: I: the entries of this reason
rules.reason: closed: incoming, no-marker, invalid-marker, member-missing, not-a-folder, link

rules.version: as import-refused; data-fed (the discarded folder's staged.json)

size: a line is at most 226 bytes without its two LFs (import-refused with every key at its cap and an 8-byte OS token: i54), so none reaches the frame's 256
formatter: record 4.5 "What the formatter writes" (T6.0 fix 4, which ruled the five points T6.0b had asked): the formatter takes each key's first value that the key's rule or list admits, drops every other value, and checks each key alone, never one key against another; a line is not written only for an unregistered event or a line over 256 bytes. A version that fails V (no SemVer, or over 24 bytes) is dropped; the caller passes `unknown` itself for a valid version of 25 to 64 bytes. A link beside another code and a code beside another reason are written as given (the pairing is the service's duty). A syscall that fails C is dropped. A count is passed as its decimal text and kept only when it passes I

emit.how: `line` is the exact line the writer emits for the event and `fields` (platform and time are inputs; platform win32 unless given). `fields` holds what the formatter is handed for the event's keys, before the token rules: a count as its decimal text, a version as text. Where a vector has `run`, it is what the run knew and the caller turned into the field beside it: `run.version` is a valid version of 25 to 64 bytes, for which the caller passes `unknown`. A value its key's rule refuses, and a key the event does not name, never reaches the file (5.3 "Registered events only"); the frame drops that field and still writes the line
